㊥ ("let's go with that") Ruling recorded: the port-or-standing distinction becomes an explicit declaration on the kind table and a flag on each act, not membership in the adjacency keys. Writing the packet now; the code work goes to an idle seat in parallel with codex-70's recompute, and the live reload waits until that recompute has finished.㊢ (ruling, carried out) Recorded in the mission Checkpoint and dispatched as packet 2726fe4e to codex-67, job `invoke-1791694546878-4269-833548ab`, park `park-262d32a4`, deadline 60 min; running. codex-70's live recompute keeps running beside it on its own seat.

🈖 (what the packet declares) The kernel gets an explicit `port-kinds` set: propose, ask-action, offer, delegate, promise, report-problem, clarify, verify. `constrain` is not in it and its adjacency row goes. Every act the adapter builds carries two flags, `:port?` and `:standing?`, stamped from the tables, and the kernel's open-port relation reads the act's flag rather than testing kind membership. So a later reading can mark one particular proposal as not awaiting a reply without touching the table, which is the future-proofing you chose. A consistency test ties the two declarations together: every adjacency key is a port kind and every port kind has a row. The tests include the bad case: a constraint is never open, yet it is in force until withdrawn.

㊟ (sequence) Code and tests only in this packet. The reload into the running service and the recompute wait until codex-70's recompute finishes, so the two passes do not interleave on the same records. Expected effect at that point: the 111 open constraints leave the inbox and the labelled session shows its four closes with both constraint rows gone.

㊭ (then) Placeholder-session records and the seven zero-act records, each a small packet; then faults as report-problem acts with claude-15.
